source.title: A p-adic Simpson correspondence for smooth proper rigid varieties
readSections: The published version (open access, CC BY 4.0), read in full: 52 pages (pp. 261–312), SHA-256 7608fff18ccbc47b96bd54cfe01f31f8ccd9953889834cc9f6c39787563175cd, fetched from link.springer.com on 29 September 2026. Received 29 August 2023, accepted 24 January 2025, published online 10 February 2025. Item locators are the journal's pages. Every recorded mistake was checked on a page image, and the exp/log valuations in E4 were recomputed exactly.

sourceVersions.note: Read by the review (REV-PAPER-HEUER-25), since Springer served the review a JavaScript challenge instead of the PDF. arXiv v3 is dated 21 January 2025, three days before acceptance; E5–E13 are scoped to it.

summary: Heuer constructs a global p-adic Simpson correspondence: for any smooth proper rigid space X over a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, a B_dR^+/ξ²-lift of X and an exponential for K give an exact tensor equivalence between vector bundles on the pro-étale site and Higgs bundles, compatible with cohomology (RΓ_proét(V) = Dolbeault cohomology). This extends Faltings from curves to all dimensions and to rigid spaces, with weaker choices. The method twists by invertible modules over the spectral algebra B of a Higgs field: a multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequence 0 → Pic_{X′} → Pic_{B,proét} → H^0(X, B ⊗ Ω̃) ⊗ G_a → 0, a representable reduction of structure group, rigidifications at points, and the exponential of p-divisible rigid groups produce L_B with HTlog(L_B) = τ_B; Rodríguez Camargo's canonical Higgs field gives the inverse. The pro-étale site, Kiehl finiteness, the Faltings extension (P8:local-rational), almost purity and the étale site of a diamond are planned; Scholze's R^nν_*Ô, the primitive comparison and pro-étale base change go to PadicHodgeTheory P8, Kedlaya–Liu to DiamondsAndVStacks D2, coherent base change and formal models to AdicSpacesPartII R2–R3, Higgs bundles to HodgeStructuresPartII, p-torsion proper base change to the mod-p Part II of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology, and the correspondence itself becomes a Part II of PadicHodgeTheory. Thirteen mistakes are recorded after review, all confirmed: a gap in the convergence radius of Lemma 5.7 for p ≥ 3 (E4) and twelve misprints, nine of them (E5–E13) found by the review in arXiv v3.

items.name: Scholze's pro-étale site with its completed structure sheaf
items.statement: For a rigid space X over K (complete, algebraically closed, over Q_p), X_proét is Scholze's (flattened) pro-étale site with the completed structure sheaf O = Ô and integral subsheaf O^+; ν : X_proét → X_ét and λ : X_proét → X_an are the natural morphisms; affinoid perfectoid objects, including toric towers over toric charts, form a basis.
items.locator: §2.1, pp. 267–268; proof of Proposition 2.9, p. 273 (published version)
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII R4 re-exports, for rigid spaces, the pro-étale site of Scholze [36, §3], which AdicEtaleGeometry A1 constructs. PadicHodgeTheory P8:local-rational plans the sheaves O_X, O_X^+, Ô_X^+ and Ô_X on X_proét and the affinoid perfectoid basis ([36, Cor. 4.7, Prop. 4.8]). AInfCohomology AI.3 builds these sheaves only on generic fibres of smooth formal schemes.

items.name: Pro-étale vector bundles, and their agreement with v-vector bundles
items.statement: A pro-étale vector bundle on X is a finite locally free Ô-module on X_proét. Vector bundles agree on all versions of the pro-étale site and on the v-site ([27, Thm. 3.5.8], Kedlaya–Liu).

items.name: Higgs bundles on a smooth rigid space
items.statement: With Ω̃_X := Ω^1_X(−1) and Ω̃^k = ∧^kΩ̃, a Higgs bundle is (E, θ) with E an analytic vector bundle and θ : E → E ⊗ Ω̃_X O_X-linear with θ ∧ θ = 0; equivalently an O_X-algebra map T_X := Sym^•Ω̃^∨ → End(E).
items.locator: Definition 1.2(2), p. 262; Definition 2.1, p. 267; Definition 4.1, p. 297 (published version)

items.name: Exponentials for K
items.statement: The p-adic exponential exp : p^αm_K → 1 + p^αm_K (α = 1/(p−1) for p ≥ 3, α = 2 for p = 2) and logarithm log : 1 + m_K → K (surjective, K algebraically closed). An exponential for K is a homomorphism Exp : K → 1 + m_K with log∘Exp = id restricting to exp on p^αm_K; one always exists ([24, Lemma 6.2]).

items.name: B_dR^+/ξ²-lifts and their existence for proper spaces
items.statement: A B_dR^+/ξ²-lift of X is a flat formal thickening 𝕏 of X over B_dR^+/ξ²; for proper smooth X such a lift exists ([16, Prop. 7.4.4], Guo), and a model over a discretely valued L ⊆ K with perfect residue field gives a canonical one.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 261; §1.3, pp. 264–265; Definition 2.12, p. 275 (published version)

items.name: Scholze's Hodge–Tate comparison for smooth rigid spaces
items.statement: For smooth X, R^nν_*Ô = Ω̃^n_X = Ω^n_X(−n) ([37, Prop. 3.23]). For proper X, not necessarily smooth, H^n_ét(X, F_p) is finite and H^n_ét(X, F_p) ⊗ O_K/p → H^n_ét(X, O^+/p) is an almost isomorphism ([37, Thm. 3.17]); for smooth proper X this is the primitive comparison theorem [36, Thm. 5.1], giving RΓ(X_proét, Ô) = RΓ_ét(X, Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} K. In particular H^1_ét(X′, μ_p) is finite for the possibly singular spectral variety X′ of Corollary 2.19.
items.locator: §1.2, (1), p. 263; proofs of Proposition 2.9(ii), p. 274, and Corollary 2.19, p. 279 (published version)
items.note: Review: the finiteness is needed for the proper, possibly singular X′, which [37, Thm. 3.17] covers. The Hodge–Tate decomposition induced by a B_dR^+/ξ²-lift (§1.2, (1)) was removed from this item: it is the case V = O of Theorem 5.5 (item 43), and the Hodge–Tate spectral-sequence comparison is planned at CohomologyComparisons CP.3; keeping it here would make route 1 depend on the lifts of route 4. ZAVYALOV-25's accepted route 7 sends R^1ν_*Ô and the primitive comparison to P8.

items.name: The Faltings extension
items.statement: Faltings's extension 0 → O → E → ν*Ω̃^1_X → 0 on X_proét ([36, Cor. 6.14]).
items.note: Review: planned at PadicHodgeTheory P8:local-rational, whose node poincare-lemma-and-faltings-extension states it for X smooth over a discretely valued field, the setting of Remark 2.17. The remark's duality with the class of the Higgs–Tate torsor L_𝕏 moved to item 21, where L_𝕏 is defined.

items.name: The rigid analytic Picard functor
items.statement: For proper X, Pic_X : Rig^sm_{K,ét} → Ab is the étale sheafification of Y ↦ H^1_an(X × Y, O^×) (analytic or étale topology, [14, Prop. 8.2.3]). It is conjectured to be a smooth rigid group; for algebraisable X = X_0^an it is Pic_{X_0}^an (Grothendieck–Murre–Oort representability and Köpf's relative GAGA).

items.name: Kiehl's proper mapping theorem
items.statement: For proper X, coherent cohomology H^i(X, B) is finite-dimensional over K.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.5, p. 287; §2.3, p. 274 (published version)

items.name: Rigid and pro-étale cohomology and base change
items.statement: For X proper and Y smooth, H^0(X × Y, Ω̃_{X×Y} ⊗ B) = (H^0(X, Ω̃_X ⊗ B) ⊗ O(Y)) ⊕ (H^0(Y, Ω̃_Y) ⊗ B(X)) ([22, Cor. 3.10, Thm. 3.18(b)]).
items.note: Review: the pro-étale clause (6) of the extracted item is now item 44 (route 1), since the pro-étale site and Ô are downstream of R3.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: integral models of coherent algebras
items.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact smooth rigid space over K and B a coherent O_X-module on X_an (the standing hypotheses of §2.3). There is a finitely presented O^+_X-module B_0 with B_0[1/p] ≅ B. It can be chosen to be an O^+_X-algebra when B is an O_X-algebra, using a finite formal model of the finite morphism Spa_{O_X}(B) → X ([7], [1, Prop. 5.9.17, Thm. 2.11.5]); for modules use [1, Prop. 4.8.18(ii)]. Set B^+ := B_0/B_0[p^∞], the image of B_0 → B on X_ét. Since B_0 may have unbounded p-torsion, B^+ need not be coherent.

items.name: Proposition 2.18: proper base change for the étale cohomology of a proper rigid space
items.statement: For g : Z → Spa(K) proper, R^mg_{ét*}(Z/nZ) = H^m_ét(Z, Z/nZ) as sheaves on Rig^sm_{K,ét} (rigid proper base change, [6, Thm. 3.15]).
items.note: Review: DiamondEtaleCohomology C5 plans proper base change only when the map is quasi-pro-étale or the coefficients have a prime-to-p annihilator, and the paper uses p-power coefficients (R^2π′_*μ_p in Corollary 2.19) for a proper map that is not quasi-pro-étale. No layer plans this case; it joins ZAVYALOV-25's mod-p Part II of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology (route 6).

items.name: Exactness of finite pushforward
items.statement: For a finite morphism f : Y′ → Y of rigid spaces, f_{ét*} is exact ([26, Prop. 2.6.3]), so H^n_ét(Y, f_*O^×) = H^n_ét(Y′, O^×) (Lemma 2.20).

items.name: Banach open mapping theorem
items.statement: A surjective continuous linear map of Banach spaces over K is open.

items.name: Fargues's analytic p-divisible rigid groups
items.statement: For a commutative rigid group G, Lie G = Hom(G_a^+, G)[1/p] ([13, Cor. 4]); an étale isogeny with finite kernel is finite étale ([13, Lemme 1, 5]); the topological p-torsion subsheaf Ĝ = Hom(Z_p, G) is an open subgroup ([21, Prop. 2.14]), an analytic p-divisible group when [p] is surjective ([24, Prop. 6.10]), with logarithm 0 → G[p^∞] → Ĝ → Lie(G) ⊗ G_a → 0.
items.locator: §3.3, p. 293; proof of Lemma 2.23, p. 282 (published version)

items.name: Theorem 3.20 (Heuer–Werner–Zhang): exponentials of rigid groups
items.statement: If G is a commutative rigid group with [p] surjective on K-points, an exponential Exp for K induces a continuous splitting Exp_G : Lie(G) → Ĝ(K) of log_G, functorial in G ([24, Thm. 6.12]).

items.name: Definition 2.2: the pro-étale Picard functor of a coherent algebra
items.statement: For X a proper rigid space over K, B a (commutative) coherent O_X-algebra on X_ét and B = ν*B, Pic_{B,proét} is the étale sheafification of S ↦ H^1_proét(X × S, B^×)/H^1_proét(S, π_{S,proét*}B^×) on Rig^sm_{K,ét}; X′ = Spa_{O_X}(B) → X is the associated finite cover (the spectral variety when B comes from a Higgs field).

items.name: Lemma 2.8: comparison modulo p^k and the exponential
items.statement: B/p^kB^+ = ν^{−1}(B/p^kB^+) on X_proét, so Rν_*(B/p^kB^+) = B/p^kB^+; for B an algebra, B^×/(1 + pB^+) = ν^{−1}(B^×/(1 + pB^+)); and exp : pB^+ ≅ 1 + pB^+ (p > 2; 4B^+ ≅ 1 + 4B^+ for p = 2).

items.name: Proposition 2.9: pushforward of ν*B and of its units
items.statement: For a coherent O_X-module B on smooth X: ν*B = Lν*B; R^nν_*B = B ⊗ Ω̃^n_X; and for an algebra, ν_*B^× = B^×, R^nν_*B^× = B ⊗ Ω̃^n_X for n ≥ 1.

items.name: Corollary 2.11: additive and multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequences
items.statement: Left-exact sequences 0 → H^1_ét(X, B) → H^1_proét(X, B) → H^0(X, Ω̃ ⊗ B) (HT_B) and 0 → H^1_ét(X, B^×) → H^1_proét(X, B^×) → H^0(X, Ω̃ ⊗ B) (HTlog), functorial in X and B.

items.name: Definitions 2.12–2.14 and Lemmas 2.13, 2.16: the Higgs–Tate torsor
items.statement: For a flat B_dR^+/ξ²-lift 𝕏, L_𝕏 ⊆ Hom(λ^{−1}O_𝕏, B_dR^+/ξ²) (lifts of λ^{−1}O_X → O) is a ν*Ω̃^∨-torsor on X_proét, natural in (X, 𝕏) (analogue of Abbes–Gros's Higgs–Tate torsor); pushing out along θ : Ω̃^∨ → B gives L_{𝕏,B,θ}. On a toric chart it is given by the cocycle γ ↦ Σ c_i(γ)∂_i. When X has a model X_0 over a discretely valued L ⊆ K with perfect residue field and 𝕏 = X_0 ×_L B_dR^+/ξ², the class of L_𝕏 is dual to the Faltings extension (item 7) (Remark 2.17, stated with a sketch).

items.name: Proposition 2.15: the lift splits the Hodge–Tate sequence
items.statement: θ ↦ [L_{𝕏,B,θ}] is a natural section s_{𝕏,B} : H^0(X, B ⊗ Ω̃) → H^1_proét(X, B) of HT_B, functorial in X and B.

items.name: Theorem 2.4 (Theorem 1.5): the multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequence of B
items.statement: For X smooth proper and B a coherent O_X-algebra: (1) 0 → Pic_{X′} → Pic_{B,proét} → H^0(X, B ⊗ Ω̃) ⊗ G_a → 0 is exact on Rig^sm_{K,ét}, functorially in B and X; (2) it splits over an open subgroup. If Pic_{X′} is representable (e.g. X algebraisable): (3) the sequence is one of rigid groups; (4) on Lie algebras it is the Hodge–Tate sequence 0 → H^1_an(X, B) → H^1_proét(X, B) → H^0(X, B ⊗ Ω̃) → 0; (5) [p] is finite étale on the identity component. On K-points, 0 → Pic(X′) → H^1_proét(X, B^×) → H^0(X, B ⊗ Ω̃) → 0 (Remark 2.22).
items.locator: Theorem 2.4, p. 269; proofs pp. 274–282; Remark 2.22, p. 281 (published version)

items.name: Corollary 2.19 and Lemma 2.21: the boundary map vanishes
items.statement: If Pic_{X′} is representable, [p] : Pic^0_{X′} → Pic^0_{X′} is a finite étale H^1_ét(X′, μ_p)-torsor; a map from a connected rigid space to a sheaf that is a quotient of a locally constant sheaf is constant, which kills ∂ : H^0(X, B ⊗ Ω̃) ⊗ G_a → R^2π′_{ét*}O^×.

items.name: Lemma 2.23: the Lie algebra of the Picard variety
items.statement: If Pic_{X′} is representable, Lie Pic_{X′} = H^1_an(X′, O) = H^1_an(X, B) (via Fargues's Lie G = Hom(G_a^+, G)[1/p] and Gerritzen's analysis of homomorphisms G_a^+ → Pic).

items.name: Theorem 3.2: a representable reduction of structure group
items.statement: With the natural splitting e_𝕏 : A_B → Pic_{B,proét}[1/p] of HTlog[1/p] given by exponentiating L_{𝕏,B} (Definition 3.1), P_𝕏 := eq(can, e_𝕏∘HTlog) sits in 0 → Pic_{X′}[p^∞] → P_𝕏 → A_B → 0, always representable by rigid groups, Lie P_𝕏 = A_B(K), with P^0_𝕏 p-divisible and HTlog : P^0_𝕏 → A_B surjective.

items.name: Lemmas 3.3–3.4: units of finite K-algebras
items.statement: For a finite K-algebra A with connected spectrum and nilradical η(A), (A ⊗ R)^× ≅ (η(A) ⊗ R) × R^× functorially; for A ↪ A′ finite, (A ⊗ O)^× is represented by G_a^r × G_m^s and (A ⊗ O)^× → (A′ ⊗ O)^× is split injective with cokernel of the same form, also on S_proét.

items.name: Lemma 3.5 and Definition 3.6: rigidifying sets of points
items.statement: For B an O_X-torsion-free coherent O_X-module on smooth proper X there is a finite M ⊆ X(K) with H^0(X, B) ↪ ∏_{x∈M} B|_x (generic freeness, [8, 051S]); torsion-freeness is needed (O_X/I² on P^1), and one point need not suffice (line bundles on P^1). Multisets and subsets of X(B_dR^+/ξ²) are B-rigidifying if their reductions are.

items.name: Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.8
items.statement: For B an O_X-torsion-free coherent O_X-algebra on the smooth proper rigid space X and S ∈ Rig^sm_K: Pic_{B,proét}(S) = H^1_proét(X × S, B^×)/H^1_proét(S, π_*B^×) = H^0(S, R^1π_{S*}B^×) without sheafification (Proposition 3.7); for a B-rigidifying multiset M the specialisation H^0(X × S, B) → ∏_{x∈M} B|_x ⊗ O(S) is injective, and Q_M = (∏_{x∈M} B|_x ⊗ O)^×/H^0(X × S, B^×) is a sheaf represented by G_a^r × G_m^s (Lemma 3.8).

items.name: Rigidified invertible B-modules and their Picard functors
items.statement: An M-rigidified invertible B-module is (L, (α_x : L|_x ≅ B|_x)_{x∈M}); isomorphisms between rigidified modules are unique (Lemma 3.11); Pic^M_{B,proét} is a sheaf (Lemma 3.13) and P^M_𝕏 its fibre over P_𝕏.

items.name: Theorem 3.14: rigidified Picard functors
items.statement: For B torsion-free and M rigidifying: 0 → Q_M → Pic^M_{B,proét} → Pic_{B,proét} → 0 is exact on Rig^sm_{K,ét} (so Pic^M is representable when Pic_{B,proét} is), and 0 → Q_M → P^M_𝕏 → P_𝕏 → 0 is exact on Rig^sm_{K,an}, so P^M_𝕏 is always a rigid group.

items.name: Additive rigidified functors and the canonical Lie algebra section
items.statement: LP^M_𝕏 parametrises (a, [(α_x)]) with a : S → A_B and rigidifications of a*L_{𝕏,B}; 0 → LQ_M → LP^M_𝕏 → A_B → 0 with LP^M_𝕏 a rigid vector group (Lemma 3.16); Lie P^M_𝕏 = LP^M_𝕏(K) functorially (Lemma 3.17); lifts x̃ ∈ X(B_dR^+/ξ²) give a section s_{𝕏,M} : A_B(K) → Lie P^M_𝕏 (Definition 3.18).

items.name: Theorem 3.22: exponential invertible B-modules
items.statement: Given a lift 𝕏 and an exponential Exp, every O_X-coherent O_X-torsion-free T_X-algebra B gets an invertible ν*B-module L_B with HTlog(L_B) = τ_B (the tautological section of Definition 3.21; its class is Exp(τ_B)), natural in B, in (X, 𝕏, K, Exp) and compatible with the product B_3 of B_1 and B_2 (τ_{B_3} = τ_{B_1} ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ τ_{B_2}), all up to unique isomorphism via rigidifications.
items.locator: Definition 3.21 and Theorem 3.22, pp. 294–297; Remark 3.23 (published version)

items.name: Definition 4.1: the spectral algebra of a Higgs field
items.statement: For a Higgs bundle (E, θ), B_θ ⊆ End(E) is the image of T_X → End(E), a commutative coherent O_X-algebra, with τ_θ ∈ H^0(X, B_θ ⊗ Ω̃) mapping to θ; enlarging B through any coherent quotient of T_X does not change ν*E ⊗_B L_B (Remark 4.2).

items.name: Toric charts, ρ_f and smallness
items.statement: A toric chart f : U → T^d (rational localisations and finite étale maps) gives the Δ = Z_p(1)^d-torsor Ũ → U and ρ_f : H^0(U, Ω̃) ≅ Hom(Δ, O(U)) (γ_i ↦ ∂_i); small pro-étale and Higgs bundles as in [20, §6], every bundle being small étale-locally.
items.note: The toric chart itself is the setting of PadicHodgeTheory P8's node cohomology-of-graded-structural-de-rham-sheaf (an étale map to T^n composed of rational embeddings and finite étale maps), which the owner imports; the isomorphism ρ_f and the notion of smallness, which the paper only cites from Heuer's Moduli spaces in p-adic non-abelian Hodge theory, are what is missing (review).

items.name: Theorem 4.4: the local correspondence (Faltings; Heuer)
items.statement: For toric U with chart f there is an exact equivalence LS_f between small pro-étale vector bundles and small Higgs bundles, sending (E, θ) to V with V(Ũ) = O(Ũ) ⊗ E(U) and γ·(a ⊗ x) = γ(a) ⊗ exp(ρ_f(θ)(γ))x ([12, §3], [20, Thm. 6.5]); ν_*End(V) is coherent (Corollary 4.5).

items.name: Lemma 4.6 and Proposition 4.7: the local correspondence as twisting
items.statement: Let B be a coherent O_X-algebra, B := ν*B, and L an invertible B-module on X_proét with τ := HTlog(L) ∈ H^0(X, Ω̃ ⊗ B). There is an étale cover of X by toric U with charts f such that ρ_f(τ|_U) : Δ → B(U) has image in 2pB^+(U), where exp converges, and L|_U is isomorphic to the invertible B-module L_{τ|U,f} obtained by descent along Ũ → U from B(Ũ) = O(Ũ) ⊗_{O(U)} B(U) with Δ-action γ·(a ⊗ x) = γ(a) ⊗ exp(ρ_{f,B}(τ|_U)(γ))x (Lemma 4.6). In the setting of Theorem 4.4, for a Higgs bundle (E, θ) with B = B_θ, there is, over an étale cover of U, a natural isomorphism LS_f^{-1}(E, θ) ≅ ν*E ⊗_B L_{τ_θ,f} (Proposition 4.7).

items.name: Theorem 4.8 and Corollaries 4.10–4.11: the canonical Higgs field (Rodríguez Camargo)
items.statement: Every pro-étale vector bundle V has a unique Higgs field θ_V : V → V ⊗ Ω̃ on X_proét, functorial in V and X, given on toric charts by the tautological Higgs field of LS_f(V), with θ_V = 0 iff V is étale-locally trivial ([34, Thm. 1.0.3]); for V = ν*E ⊗_B L with HTlog(L) = τ_B, θ_V = ν*θ_E ⊗_B L.

items.name: Definition 4.12 and Proposition 4.13: untwisting a pro-étale bundle
items.statement: θ_V gives a coherent O_X-algebra B_V ⊆ ν_*End(V) with section τ_{B_V}; for any invertible ν*B_V-module L with HTlog(L) = τ_{B_V}, V ⊗ L^{−1} is an analytic vector bundle with Higgs field θ_V ⊗ L^{−1}.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (Theorem 1.1): the p-adic Simpson correspondence
items.statement: For X smooth proper over K, a B_dR^+/ξ²-lift 𝕏 and an exponential Exp give an exact tensor equivalence S_{𝕏,Exp} : {pro-étale vector bundles on X} ≅ {Higgs bundles on X}, V ↦ ν_*((V, θ_V) ⊗ L_{B_V}^{−1}), with inverse (E, θ) ↦ ν*E ⊗ L_{B_θ}, natural in (X, 𝕏, K, Exp). For connected X and x ∈ X(K) this gives a fully faithful exact tensor functor Rep_K(π_1(X, x)) → Higgs bundles.
items.locator: Theorem 5.1, p. 304; proof pp. 304–306; Theorem 1.1 and §1.1, pp. 261–262 (published version)

items.name: Proposition 5.3: deformation to the Higgs bundle
items.statement: For V and (E, θ) = S_{𝕏,Exp}(V) there are a connected smooth rigid S with points 0, s and a pro-étale vector bundle N on X × S with N|_{X×0} ≅ ν*E and N|_{X×s} ≅ V.

items.name: Dolbeault cohomology of a Higgs bundle
items.statement: For a Higgs bundle (E, θ) on a smooth rigid space X of dimension d, C*_Higgs(E, θ) = [E → E ⊗ Ω̃^1 → ··· → E ⊗ Ω̃^d] with θ_k(e ⊗ w) = θ(e) ∧ w, and RΓ_Higgs(X, (E, θ)) := RΓ(X_ét, C*_Higgs(E, θ)). As complexes on X_ét, C*_Higgs(E, θ) = RHom_{T_X}(O_X, E) for the T_X-module structure given by θ, computed by the Koszul resolution K• of O_X over T_X; hence RΓ_Higgs(X, (E, θ)) = RΓ(X_ét, RHom_{T_X}(O_X, E)).

items.name: Theorem 5.5 (Theorem 1.4): the cohomological comparison
items.statement: For V and (E, θ) = S_{𝕏,Exp}(V) there is a natural isomorphism Rν_*V = C^*_Higgs(E, θ) in D(X_ét), hence RΓ(X_proét, V) = RΓ_Higgs(X, (E, θ)); for V = O it recovers the Hodge–Tate decomposition. The proof lifts L_B to the completion T̂_J and compares Koszul complexes with continuous group cohomology of Δ (Lemma 5.7, via [20, Lemma 6.7]); see E4 for the radius needed.
items.locator: Theorem 5.5 and Lemma 5.7, pp. 307–310; Theorem 1.4, p. 263 (published version)

items.name: Pro-étale base change for a coherent algebra over a proper space
items.statement: For X proper, Y smooth and a coherent O_X-module B, π_{Y*}B = B(X) ⊗_K O_{Y_proét} on Y_proét ([22, Thm. 3.18(c)]), where π_Y : X × Y → Y.
items.note: Added in review, split from item 10: it is a statement on the pro-étale site with its completed structure sheaf, which is downstream of AdicSpacesPartII R3. PadicHodgeTheory P8 plans the analogous relative base change for gr^0 OB_dR (PAPER-SCHOLZE-13/s8-lem8.6).

items.name: The étale site of a rigid space and of its diamond
items.statement: For a rigid space X, the functor Y ↦ Y^◇ induces an equivalence between the étale sites of X and of its diamond X^◇ ([38, Lemma 15.6]).
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 2.4(3) and Theorem 3.2 (arXiv v3; cited as [38, Lemma 15.6])

items.name: Continuous group cohomology on a toric chart
items.statement: For a toric smooth affinoid U with toric chart f and a small pro-étale vector bundle V on U, the continuous cohomology of the toric Galois group Δ ≅ Z_p(1)^d computes pro-étale cohomology, H^n_cts(Δ, V(Ũ)) = H^n(U_proét, V), through the Cartan–Leray sequence for the pro-finite-étale Δ-torsor Ũ → U.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.7 (arXiv v3; the paper cites [21, Lemma 6.7])
items.note: Added in review. The comparison of Koszul complexes in Lemma 5.7 rests on it and no item states it; P8 plans the case V = Ô.

items.name: Almost purity
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra (R, R^+) and a finite étale R-algebra S, S is perfectoid and S°a is finite étale over R°a ([35, Thm. 7.9(iii)]); hence for a pro-finite-étale map Spa(D, D^+) → Spa(C, C^+) of affinoid perfectoids, C^+/p^k → D^+/p^k is a filtered colimit of almost finite étale maps.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.9(i) (arXiv v3; cited there as [35, Thm. 5.2], see E6)
items.note: Added in review. PerfectoidSpaces P3 plans ECD Theorem 6.1 (almost purity and étale tilting).

items.name: Pro-étale cohomology of pulled-back étale sheaves
items.statement: For an abelian sheaf F on X_ét and a quasi-compact quasi-separated U = lim U_j in X_proét, H^i(U, ν^{-1}F) = colim_j H^i(U_j, F); consequently F → Rν_*ν^{-1}F is an isomorphism ([36, Lemma 3.16, Cor. 3.17]).
items.note: Added in review. PAPER-SCHOLZE-13 marks [36, Lemma 3.16] and Corollary 3.17 planned in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 (continuity under cofiltered limits); this item follows it.

routes.reason: P8 owns the relative period sheaves and their proper-smooth comparison suffix: Scholze's R^nν_*Ô = Ω̃^n, the primitive comparison and finiteness (item 6), and the pro-étale base change of item 44. PAPER-ZAVYALOV-25's accepted route 7 (its items 58 and 116), PAPER-SCHOLZE-13's route 1 and PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18's route 14 are the precedents. As corrected in review (REV-PAPER-HEUER-25), the Faltings extension (item 7) is planned at P8:local-rational and the Hodge–Tate decomposition at CohomologyComparisons CP.3; the clauses that need the B_dR^+/ξ²-lifts or the Higgs–Tate torsor, which route 4 builds on top of P8, moved to route 4. The earlier precedent, PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17, placed its Faltings extension in a route that its review rejected.

D2 owns the pro-étale and v-topologies with v-descent; Kedlaya–Liu's agreement of vector bundles across the pro-étale sites and the v-site is a descent statement of that layer. Review: the v-site of X should be taken as perfectoid spaces over X (Perf_K/X), which D2 builds; the diamond X^◇ is DiamondsAndVStacks D6's, and D6 requires D2.

R2 owns formal models and R3 coherent sheaves with Kiehl-type finiteness, coherence and base change. Item 11 (Lemma 2.7) is an R3 statement on X_an using R2's finite formal models, and item 10 is coherent base change for proper spaces. As corrected in review (REV-PAPER-HEUER-25), the pro-étale clause of item 10 moved to route 1 (item 44), since the pro-étale site is downstream of R3; B^+ on X_ét and X_proét is item 18, in route 4.

routes.title: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison, Part II: the p-adic Simpson correspondence for smooth proper rigid spaces
routes.brief: Extend P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) from the Hodge–Tate decomposition to non-abelian coefficients, following Heuer, A p-adic Simpson correspondence for smooth proper rigid varieties (Invent. Math. 240 (2025), 261–312). Final theorems: Theorem 5.1, for X smooth proper over a complete algebraically closed K ⊇ Q_p, a B_dR^+/ξ²-lift 𝕏 and an exponential Exp give an exact tensor equivalence between pro-étale vector bundles and Higgs bundles (θ : E → E ⊗ Ω^1(−1), θ ∧ θ = 0), natural in (X, 𝕏, K, Exp); Theorem 5.5, for V and (E, θ) = S_{𝕏,Exp}(V) there is a natural isomorphism Rν_*V = C^•_Higgs(E, θ) in D(X_ét), whose cohomology over X gives RΓ(X_proét, V) = RΓ_Higgs(X, (E, θ)); Proposition 5.3, there are a connected smooth rigid space S over K with two points 0, s ∈ S(K) and a pro-étale vector bundle N on X × S with N|_{X×{0}} ≅ ν*E and N|_{X×{s}} ≅ V. Layers: (1) Higgs bundles, spectral algebras B_θ and the tautological section τ; (2) the pro-étale Picard functor of a coherent algebra and the multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequence (Theorem 2.4), through Lemma 2.8, Proposition 2.9, Corollary 2.11, the Higgs–Tate torsor of a lift (Proposition 2.15), proper base change and the vanishing of the boundary map; (3) the reduction P_𝕏 (Theorem 3.2) and rigidified Picard functors (Lemmas 3.3–3.17, Theorem 3.14); (4) Fargues's analytic p-divisible groups and the Heuer–Werner–Zhang exponential of rigid groups, giving L_B (Theorem 3.22); (5) the local correspondence on toric charts and the canonical Higgs field of Rodríguez Camargo (§4); (6) the equivalence and the cohomological comparison (§5), using a convergence radius strictly smaller than p^{−1/(p−1)} in Lemma 5.7 (PAPER-HEUER-25/E4). Import the pro-étale site and its completed structure sheaf from Foundations of adic spaces, Part II (AdicSpacesPartII R4) and P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory P8:local-rational, which also plans the Faltings extension); the primitive comparison, R^nν_*Ô and pro-étale base change from PadicHodgeTheory P8; the Hodge–Tate decomposition from CohomologyComparisons CP.3; Kedlaya–Liu v-descent from Pro-étale descent, diamonds and small v-stacks (DiamondsAndVStacks D2) and the étale site of a diamond from D6; Kiehl finiteness, formal models and coherent base change from AdicSpacesPartII R2–R3; finite pushforward and continuity from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0; proper base change with p-power coefficients from that roadmap's mod-p Part II (route 6); almost purity from PerfectoidSpaces P3; algebraic Picard functors from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2; and twisted Higgs bundles from HodgeStructuresPartII (route 5). PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17 proposed its arithmetic p-adic Simpson functor for HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison in a route its review rejected; the comparison with it should be made once that extraction is re-routed.
routes.reason: No layer plans a p-adic Simpson correspondence or its ingredients: the multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequence, the reduction P_𝕏, rigidified Picard functors, the exponential of rigid groups, the local correspondence, the canonical Higgs field and the cohomological comparison. Twisted Higgs bundles, including the p-adic Ω^1(−1) instance, belong to the accepted HodgeStructuresPartII (PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17 route 14), which leaves the p-adic Simpson functor to others, so item 3 is routed there (route 5) and imported. The correspondence continues PadicHodgeTheory's Hodge–Tate comparison to non-abelian coefficients, so it is that roadmap's Part II; the queue groups it with the other accepted PadicHodgeTheory Part II proposals (FARGUES-FONTAINE-18 route 5, GLEASON-LIM-XU-26 route 14, GUO-REINECKE-24 route 2) in one design. As corrected in review (REV-PAPER-HEUER-25): the earlier reason credited Liu–Zhu's functor to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison, but T6:comparison plans logarithmic Riemann–Hilbert, and PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17's route 8 to it was rejected.

routes.title: Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized), Part II: variations, period maps and non-abelian Hodge theory
routes.reason: Added in review (REV-PAPER-HEUER-25). PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17's accepted route 14 proposes this Part II and defines twisted integrable Higgs bundles on ringed differential sites, noting that the p-adic instance uses Ω^1(−1); the parent, id, title and area are that route's, so the item joins its design.
routes.brief: The same Part II that PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17 proposes under this id. This paper adds the instance it needs: on a smooth rigid space X over a complete algebraically closed extension K of Q_p, with Ω̃_X := Ω^1_X(−1), a Higgs bundle is an analytic vector bundle E with an O_X-linear θ : E → E ⊗ Ω̃_X such that θ ∧ θ = 0, equivalently an O_X-algebra map Sym^•Ω̃^∨ → End(E) (Heuer, A p-adic Simpson correspondence for smooth proper rigid varieties, Definition 1.2(2)). The p-adic Simpson correspondence itself stays in PadicHodgeTheory's Part II (route 4), which imports this definition; build it on the general twisted Higgs bundles already planned here rather than as a separate notion.

routes.title: The classical analytic cohomology inputs to diamonds, Part II: mod-p Poincaré duality for smooth proper rigid spaces
routes.reason: Added in review (REV-PAPER-HEUER-25). DiamondEtaleCohomology C5 plans proper base change only for quasi-pro-étale maps or prime-to-p coefficients, and no layer plans the p-torsion case for rigid spaces. PAPER-ZAVYALOV-25's accepted route 1 proposes this Part II for étale cohomology of rigid spaces with p-torsion coefficients; the parent, id, title and area are that route's, so the item joins its design.
routes.brief: The same Part II that PAPER-ZAVYALOV-25 proposes under this id, for mod-p étale cohomology of rigid spaces. This paper adds one input it uses: rigid-analytic proper base change with torsion coefficients, including p-power torsion, in the form of Bhatt–Hansen, The six functors for Zariski-constructible sheaves in rigid geometry, Theorem 3.15: for g : Z → Spa(K) proper and every n, m ∈ N, R^mg_{ét*}(Z/nZ) = H^m_ét(Z, Z/nZ) as sheaves on smooth rigid spaces over K (Heuer, Proposition 2.18). Heuer applies it with n a power of p in the Kummer sequences of §2.6. Build it with the other p-torsion finiteness and duality results of this Part II, importing Huber's proper-support theory from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H3.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.7, pp. 308–310 (for p ≥ 3) (published version)
sourceIssues.printed: It defines T̂_U := O_U⟨p^{−α}∂_1, …, p^{−α}∂_d⟩ and introduces c : Δ → T̂_U^×(U) by γ_i ↦ exp(∂_i). It claims an isomorphism with inverse T ↦ exp(∂) − 1, and asserts log(T + 1)/T belongs to the units R⟨p^{−α}T⟩^×.
sourceIssues.correction: Use a convergence radius |p|^β with β > 1/(p − 1) (for example β = 1 when p ≥ 3; for p = 2 the paper's α = 2 already works), after a further étale localisation making E and V small for that radius.
sourceIssues.reason: With α = 1/(p − 1), the Tate algebra O_U⟨p^{−α}∂⟩ is the closed disc |∂| ≤ |p|^{1/(p−1)}, where exp does not converge: in the variable y = p^{−α}∂ the coefficient of y^{p^k} in exp(∂) has valuation exactly 1/(p − 1) for every k, so exp(∂_i) ∉ T̂_U. Likewise log(1 + T)/T, with T = p^αz, has a unit coefficient at z^{p−1} (it vanishes at T = ζ_p − 1, which lies on that disc), so it is not a unit in R⟨p^{−α}T⟩ and T ↦ exp(∂) − 1 is not defined. The comparison of Koszul complexes goes through on any strictly smaller disc. Theorem 5.5 is not in doubt; the same comparison appears in [5] and [20].

review.reason: Checked in arXiv v3 and recomputed. §3.3 defines exp on the open disc p^α m_K with α = 1/(p−1), but the proof of Lemma 5.7 works in O_U⟨p^{−α}∂⟩, the closed disc. In y = p^{−α}∂ the coefficient of y^n in exp(∂) has valuation s_p(n)/(p − 1), which is 1/(p − 1) at n = p^k for every k, so exp(∂_i) is not in T_U; and with T = p^α z, log(1 + T)/T has the unit coefficient 1 at z^{p−1}, vanishing at T = ζ_p − 1 on that disc. For p = 2, α = 2 exceeds 1/(p − 1) and the argument works. Any radius |p|^β with β > 1/(p − 1) repairs it; Theorem 5.5 stands. The published text was not re-read in review (Springer served a JavaScript challenge); checked in arXiv 2307.01303v3.
